summary: Iter 84h (Footfall — Outside Traffic + Turn-in Rate) verified end-to-end. Backend: 4/4 pytest pass — /api/footfall returns outside_traffic + turn_in_rate per row; /api/footfall/weekday-pattern returns avg_outside_traffic + avg_turn_in_rate + total_outside_window per row AND in group_avg_by_weekday entries. Frontend: KPI strip now has 6 cards including ff-kpi-outside (Outside Traffic = 4,740) and ff-kpi-turnin (Turn-in Rate = 17.4%, displayed in green pill which is correct for ≥15%). Per-store breakdown table has new OUTSIDE TRAFFIC and TURN-IN columns; default sort = turn-in ascending (worst first → Vivo Nakuru 4.5% at the top with red pill). 'Lowest turn-in rates →' / 'Lowest performers →' buttons on BOTH the Outside and Turn-in cards open the ff-bottom-turnin drill-down with 5 worst-performer rows and the correct headers [STORE / OUTSIDE TRAFFIC / FOOTFALL IN / TURN-IN RATE / VS LAST PERIOD]. Close button works. Weekday heatmap now has 5 modes including heatmap-mode-outside and heatmap-mode-turnin; toggling repaints cells (Vivo Nakuru: outside-mode → '1.6k/1.4k/1.7k/572', turn-in-mode → '2.3%/6.9%/4.7%/11.5%'). Existing functionality ('Which stores dropped?', Export CSV, conversion deltas, date/country/POS filters) still works.

issues: Several stores show physically-impossible turn-in rates (>100%), e.g. Zoya Sarit Sat=734.8%, Sun=626.9%; Vivo Yaya Sun=12600%; Vivo MSA Digo Road Mon=184%. Per the agent-to-agent note this is upstream BI-feed data quality (partial pavement-counter sample), NOT an iter-84h bug. Recommendation for a follow-up iteration: cap displayed turn-in at 100% (or surface a small warning icon when raw value >100%) so the user is not visually misled.

action_items: (Non-blocking, recommend) Visually cap turn-in% at 100 in heatmap and breakdown, OR badge values >100% as 'data anomaly', because the BI feed currently yields >100% on a handful of cells (Zoya Sarit, Vivo Yaya Sun, Vivo MSA Digo Road Mon, etc). Functional logic is correct; this is purely a UX safety-net.

(Non-blocking) Add a per-row data-testid on the breakdown table rows (e.g. data-testid='ff-breakdown-row-<location>') so future regression scripts can assert the per-store turn-in pill colour directly in the DOM.
critical_code_review_comments: Footfall.jsx scopedEnriched.turn_in_rate is computed as Footfall_In / Outside_Traffic * 100 client-side BUT the row also already carries the backend-supplied turn_in_rate; client code uses the recomputed version. This is fine but should be documented — the comment block at line 144 already explains this. No bug.
FootfallWeekdayHeatmap Cell component correctly renders '—' for outside/turn-in modes when hasOutside=false (line 54-63). Verified working.

Default sort initialSort={{key:'turn_in_rate', dir:'asc'}} pushes worst stores to the top of the table as required. sortValue function correctly returns 999999 for null turn-in so '—' rows fall to the bottom — good defensive coding.
